content.user_title: Build Allra JPA and QueryDSL Standards
content.value_statement: Database code can drift across entity, repository, and transaction patterns. This skill gives Allra teams a shared checklist for JPA, QueryDSL, DTO projections, and Spring transaction boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Explains the Allra QueryDSL repository support pattern.
Shows DTO projection setup with record types and QueryProjection.
Defines when to use read-only and write transactions.
Documents JPA entity fields, ID generation, timestamps, and enum mapping.
Recommends lazy association mapping and repository injection practices.
limitations: Does not execute database migrations or inspect a live schema.
Assumes Java 17, Spring Boot 3.2, JPA, and optional QueryDSL.
Requires project-specific decisions for database vendor features.
Does not replace security review for credential or tenant data handling.

use_cases.title: Design Consistent Entities
use_cases.description: Create JPA entities that follow Allra naming, mapping, timestamp, and relationship conventions.

use_cases.title: Review QueryDSL Repositories
use_cases.description: Check repository support classes, DTO projections, and query placement before merging backend changes.

use_cases.title: Audit Transaction Boundaries
use_cases.description: Verify service methods use read-only or write transactions according to their behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Entity Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a new JPA entity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this JPA entity against the Allra database schema rules. Check field constraints, lazy relationships, and timestamp fields. Summarize required changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create Repository Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design the repository interfaces and QueryDSL support class for this use case. Follow the Allra repository placement rules.

prompt_templates.title: Add Transaction Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these service methods and recommend the correct Spring transaction annotations. Separate read-only methods from methods that change state.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor QueryDSL Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup of repository and DTO projection design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this database access workflow using Allra QueryDSL standards. Address DTO projection, repository ownership, database compatibility, and dependency injection concerns.

output_examples.input: A service class has read methods and user activation methods without transaction annotations.
output_examples.output: The review separates read-only lookups from state changes and recommends transaction annotations for each public method.

output_examples.input: A repository implementation directly depends on a support implementation class.
output_examples.output: The response explains why the JPA repository interface should be injected and lists the repository structure to use.

output_examples.input: A new entity includes eager relationships and missing field constraints.
output_examples.output: The review identifies the mapping issues and recommends lazy relationships, explicit columns, and audit timestamp fields.

best_practices: Use the JPA repository interface as the service dependency.
Choose read-only transactions for query-only service methods.
Check database vendor compatibility before using special functions.
anti_patterns: Do not inject QueryDSL support implementation classes directly.
Do not place a query in a repository that does not match the main From clause.
Do not rely on default transaction behavior for public service methods.

faq.question: What projects is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for Allra backend projects that use Java, Spring Boot, JPA, Hibernate, and optional QueryDSL.

faq.question: Does it generate migrations?
faq.answer: No. It guides entity and repository design, but it does not create or run database migration files.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it to compare entities, repositories, services, and DTO projections against the documented rules.

faq.question: Does QueryDSL have to be used?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes QueryDSL as optional and allows other project-specific query approaches.

faq.question: How does it handle transactions?
faq.answer: It recommends explicit Spring transaction annotations for public service methods based on read or write behavior.

faq.question: Does it cover every database vendor?
faq.answer: No. It reminds users to check vendor support for functions, pagination behavior, and advanced SQL features.
